\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 1.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Define probability of an event. State and prove the addition law of probability for $n$ events. \pts{2+7}
  \item Two cards are drawn from a pack of ordinary playing cards. Find the probability that the second card drawn is a heart. \pts{5}
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 2.}
Explain the following terms with appropriate examples:

\begin{parts}
  \item Equally likely events \pts{3}
  \item Exhaustive events \pts{3}
  \item Mutually exclusive events \pts{3}
  \item Random experiment \pts{2}
  \item Independent and dependent events \pts{3}
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 3.}

\begin{parts}
  \item State and prove Bayes' theorem. \pts{7}
  \item In a bolt factory, machines A, B, and C manufacture 25\%, 35\%, and 40\% of the total output respectively. Of their outputs, 5\%, 4\%, and 2\% respectively are defective bolts. A bolt is taken at random and found to be defective. What is the probability that the bolt came from machine A? \pts{5}
  \item Define discrete and continuous random variables with appropriate examples. \pts{2}
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 4.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Find the probability distribution function for the number of heads when 3 balanced coins are tossed. \pts{4}
  \item Explain the concept of a random variable. What is a cumulative distribution function (c.d.f.) and what are its properties? \pts{10}
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 5.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Define mathematical expectation of a random variable. \pts{2}
  \item For what value of $A$, the function defined below will be a probability density function (p.d.f.)?
  \[
  f(x) = 
\begin{cases}
    A x^2 (1 - x), & 0 \le x \le 1 \\
    0, &  \text{otherwise}
  \end{cases}
  \]
  Also find $E(X)$, $E(X^2)$, $Var(X)$, and $P\left(\frac{1}{4} < X < \frac{1}{2}\right)$. \pts{12}
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 6.}

\begin{parts}
  \item What is a binomial experiment and what are its properties? Derive the mean and variance of a binomial distribution. \pts{10}
  \item Let $X$ have a binomial distribution with parameters $n=4$ and $p=\frac{1}{3}$. Find $P(X = 1)$ and $P(X = 3)$. \pts{4}
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 7.}

\begin{parts}
  \item Describe a Poisson distribution. Derive its mean and variance. \pts{8}
  \item Derive the recurrence relation for the moments of binomial and Poisson distributions. \pts{6}
\end{parts}
\medskip\rule{\linewidth}{0.2pt}

\medskip


\noindent   \textbf{Question 8.}
Write short notes on any   \textbf{four} of the following:

\begin{parts}
  \item Properties of a good estimator
  \item Null and alternative hypotheses, and simple and composite hypotheses
  \item Two types of errors in hypothesis testing
  \item Any one application of Chi-square statistic in significance testing
  \item Any one application of $F$-statistic in significance testing
\end{parts}
\pts{4 $ \times$ 3.5}
